SMTO-LLM-0059 — SMTO couldn't find the model server program on that computer

GUID: 9b2a6021-c16f-5b08-9096-fba389b312cd
Slug: local-ai-executable-missing
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • The program needed to run this model server isn't installed where the Gateway looks for it, so nothing was started. Installing it on a different computer won't help.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages the Gateway's computer to install the model server program your profile uses (vLLM, llama.cpp or Ollama) there. The Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses on that computer, only looks for programs on its own computer.
  2. If it's already installed in an unusual place, open the profile in Parameter Store, put the program's full location in executable, and select Save. Giving the full location lets the Gateway find a program outside its usual search folders.
  3. Ask SMTO to show the Local AI status for that Gateway and check the program now shows as installed. This confirms the Gateway can see the program before you try to start it.
  4. Start the model server again in a new message that names the profile with @. Nothing was started this time, and a new message uses the saved profile.

What success looks like

  • The Local AI status shows the program as installed, and the model server reaches ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway; the Gateway may need restarting after installing so it sees the new program.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected Gateway found no executable for the profile's provider (vllm, llama-server or ollama, or the profile's executable override) on the Gateway process's PATH, so nothing was launched.

What this means

  • Executable resolution found no matching provider binary in the configured path or Gateway environment. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • Executable resolution found no matching provider binary in the configured path or Gateway environment.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the profile executable and Gateway service account's search path; distinguish an absent file from an unsupported executable name.

How to fix it

  • Install the provider on the Gateway host so the Gateway service account's PATH resolves it, or set the profile's executable to its absolute path (the file name must still be vllm, llama-server or ollama). Restart the Gateway if you changed its PATH, then check local_ai.status.
  • Install the supported provider on that Gateway or correct the accepted profile's executable path.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The same Gateway account resolves the intended provider executable.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
